novelty_flags.label: related_work and comparator_promise_table / CortezEichhornYu2022
novelty_flags.one_line: They attribute the Bernoulli and complete-rollout unbiasedness/variance theorems to “Theorems 1 and 2,” but the NeurIPS proceedings state these as Theorems 2 and 3.

soundness_flags.label: ass:sparse-dependency-degree; thm:design-clt; thm:conservative-wald-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: D is defined only by pairwise non-independence, which is not a dependency graph: Stein dependency-graph CLTs require joint independence of any two edge-separated collections, so the stated degree condition cannot justify the claimed CLT or inherited coverage result.

soundness_flags.label: prop:quadratic-witness
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed Γ(p,r) uses p as a scalar kernel argument although p is the rollout-node vector, and r is not declared; write Γ(x,r) (or introduce a scalar stage fraction) consistently.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:exact-covariance-saddle
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The exact minimax and certificate are conditional on the newly declared aggregate-coefficient ellipsoid, a strict subclass of the full low-order bounded-outcome schedule class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact common-uniform minimax optimality under C_ellip(B,omega), not over all low-order schedules in C_CEY.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5–6, Theorems 2 and 3; lines 463–507 of proceedings extraction
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 2 gives unbiasedness and a variance order for staggered Bernoulli rollout; Theorem 3 gives the corresponding complete-randomized-rollout result.
For the positive-semidefinite ellipsoidal class M_K, the minimax criterion is C times lambda_max(K^(1/2)Q(sigma)K^(1/2)); the paper concerns two-arm assignment designs.
The paper derives an upper bound for variance/MSE of a single-stage standard HT estimator and optimizes a covariance-based surrogate.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract, lines 15–18; Section 3 is the dependency-graph CLT
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves asymptotic normality for a Horvitz–Thompson estimator under a restricted dependency-graph condition and develops a distinct difference-in-means result.
Under finite-population ANI, the network-HAC variance estimator has a bias interpretable as variance of unit-level exposure effects, yielding a conservative-inference analogue.
The paper develops design-based theory for arbitrary complex designs and procedures for consistently estimating asymptotic variance bounds.

The paper supplies a low-order pseudoinverse TTE estimator and design-dependent bias/variance bounds for general and clustered designs, rather than an optimized common-uniform rollout-node covariance saddle.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace D by a genuine dependency graph built from primitive coordinate-support sets, requiring that edge-separated collections of full stage-outcome vectors are jointly independent; then restate the degree condition and redo the CLT/coverage targets under that condition.
Correct every CortezEichhornYu2022 theorem-number reference to Theorems 2 and 3 and anchor the exact-covariance distinction to its pp. 5–6 variance-bound display.

Add an explicit finite-dimensional algorithm and complexity bound for evaluating the isotypic blocks and globally minimizing the node-weight program; this would turn the field-level certificate into a stronger constructive design result.

recommended_next_step: Revise the dependency premise and quadratic-witness notation, correct the Cortez theorem citation, then retain the exact ellipsoidal covariance saddle as the field-level kernel.
